title: Gaza Strip
description: Autonomous territory in the Middle East
wiki_lead:
The Gaza Strip, also known simply as Gaza, is the smaller of the two Palestinian territories (the other being the West Bank) that make up the State of Palestine in the Southern Levant region of West Asia. Gaza is bordered by Egypt on the southwest, Israel on the east and north, and the Mediterranean Sea to the west. Its capital and largest city is Gaza City.
The territorial boundaries were established by the Green Line of the 1949 Armistice Agreements at the conclusion of the 1948 Palestine war, at which time Gaza was controlled by the Kingdom of Egypt. During that period, the All-Palestine Protectorate, also known as All-Palestine, was established with limited recognition, and it became a refuge for Palestinians who fled or were expelled by Zionist forces in the Nakba. In the 1967 Arab–Israeli War, Israel captured and occupied the Gaza Strip among other territories, initiating a decades-long military occupation of the Palestinian territories. The mid-1990s Oslo Accords established the Palestinian Authority (PA) as a limited governing authority, initially led by the secular party Fatah until its electoral defeat in 2006 to the Sunni Islamist Hamas. Hamas would then take over the governance of Gaza in the Battle of Gaza the next year, subsequently warring with Israel.
The restrictions on movement and goods in Gaza imposed by Israel date back to the early 1990s. In 2005, Israel unilaterally withdrew its military forces from Gaza, dismantled its settlements, and implemented a temporary blockade of Gaza. The blockade became indefinite after the 2007 Hamas takeover. Egypt also began its blockade of Gaza in 2007. Despite the Israeli disengagement, Gaza was still considered occupied by Israel under international law, being described as an "open-air prison". Israel's actions in Gaza since the start of the war that began in 2023 have resulted in large-scale loss of life, mass population displacement, a humanitarian crisis, and a partial famine. These actions have been described by scholars, international law experts, and human-rights organizations as constituting a genocide against the Palestinian people. A provisional ceasefire began in mid-January 2025, lasting two months. In August, Israel began an offensive on Gaza City. By 9 October 2025, Israel and Hamas agreed to the first part of a United States-led peace plan. United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803, adopted on 17 November 2025, contains provisions for the transitional governance of the Gaza Strip.
The Gaza Strip is 41 kilometres (25 miles) long, from 6 to 12 km (3.7 to 7.5 mi) wide, and has a total area of 365 km2 (141 sq mi). In 2010, it had a population of just over 2 million, mostly of Palestinian refugees and their descendants. It is one of the most densely populated territories in the world, with a population density similar to that of cities like Tel Aviv or London. Before the Gaza war, its capital Gaza City was roughly the 90th-most densely populated city in the world, and had about a third of the population density of cities like Malé or Giza. The Gaza Strip has a high proportion of youth, with 43.5% being children 14 or younger and 50% under age of 18. Sunni Islam is almost ubiquitous, with a Palestinian Christian minority. Gaza has an annual population growth rate of 1.99% (2023 est.), the 39th-highest in the world. Gaza's unemployment rate is among the highest in the world, with an overall unemployment rate of 46% and a youth unemployment rate of 70%. Despite this, the area's 97% literacy rate is higher than that of nearby Egypt, while youth literacy is 88%. Gaza has throughout the years been seen as a source of Palestinian nationalism and resistance.

grok_lead: The Gaza Strip (Hebrew: ×¨×¦××¢×ª ×¢××; Arabic: ÙØ·Ø§Ø¹ ØºØ²Ø©) is a narrow coastal enclave in the southern Levant, measuring 41 kilometers in length and varying from 6 to 12 kilometers in width, with a total land area of 365 square kilometers bordering Israel to the north and east, Egypt to the southwest, and the Mediterranean Sea to the west. Its population, predominantly Palestinian Arabs, stood at approximately 2.1 million as of 2026, yielding one of the world's highest population densities at over 5,700 people per square kilometer, exacerbated by limited arable land and water resources. Since June 2007, following Hamas's armed seizure of power from the Fatah-led Palestinian Authority, the territory has been under the de facto control of Hamas, an Islamist militant organization designated as a terrorist group by the United States, European Union, and others, which has prioritized military buildup over civilian welfare. Following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire in October 2025, Israeli forces have expanded control to approximately 60-70% of the territory as of late 2026, with Hamas retaining influence in remaining populated areas. The Gaza District Coordination and Liaison Administration (××ª"×§) continues to implement Israeli civilian policy, coordinating resident and goods movements through crossings such as Kerem Shalom and Erez in accordance with security protocols. In response to this takeover and to curb arms imports and militant activities, Israel and Egypt have maintained a blockade restricting the flow of goods and people, leading to chronic economic stagnation, unemployment rates exceeding 40 percent pre-2023 war, and near-total reliance on international aid for basic needs. The Gaza Strip's defining characteristics include its role as a launchpad for thousands of rocket attacks and cross-border incursions against Israel by Hamas and allied groups, culminating in the October 7, 2023, assault that killed over 1,200 Israelis and precipitated Israel 's military campaign to dismantle Hamas 's governance and capabilities, resulting in extensive destruction and significant Palestinian casualties. A U.S.-brokered ceasefire took effect in October 2025, though incidents have continued and large-scale reconstruction remains limited. This cycle of violence traces back to the territory's post-1948 status under Egyptian administration until Israel 's 1967 capture, subsequent occupation until the 2005 disengagement, and persistent failure of internal Palestinian reconciliation or external diplomatic efforts to establish stable, non-militarized rule. Economically, Gaza's isolation has fostered a shadow economy reliant on smuggling tunnels and external subsidies from patrons like Qatar and Iran, while governance under Hamas has been marked by authoritarian suppression of dissent, diversion of resources to military tunnels and rockets, and limited development in education or infrastructure despite substantial aid inflows. Humanitarian assessments remain contested: COGAT data show tens of thousands of aid trucks (majority food, totaling hundreds of thousands of tons) entered Gaza, often 2-2.5 times OCHA figures that exclude non-UN, private, and Gaza Humanitarian Foundation deliveries and exceed WFP caloric needs estimates, while the UN-backed IPC declared famine (Phase 5) in Gaza Governorate in August 2025 using a 15% MUAC threshold (versus conventional 30% WHZ), hospital-biased samples, and incomplete data from Hamas-linked sources; reported malnutrition deaths stayed far below IPC's two-per-10,000 daily threshold. Hamas has attacked aid workers (including GHF) and diverted supplies, per IDF-released Gazan testimonies.
